history.summary: DEFINITE DUPLICATE: this is the SAME temple as CSV seq 1418 ('Paatal Bhairavi Temple') - the Wikipedia article for this site is titled 'Barfani Dham (Patal Bhairvi)' and the Chhattisgarh government tourism page lists 'Patal Bhairvi Temple' describing the Barfani Dham complex. It is a modern three-level temple built in the shape of a giant Shivlinga at Rajnandgaon, associated with Barfani Baba. The bottom level (16 ft below ground) is the sanctum of Maa Patal Bhairavi - a fierce 15-ft, 11-tonne idol flanked by Hanuman, Bhairav Baba and Ganesha in a circular sanctum, found during excavation per local accounts. The middle level is the Devi Lok with the Tripura Sundari/Dashamahavidya shrine. The top level holds Shiva shrines including replicas of the 12 Jyotirlingas and a 108-ft Shiva Linga, with a large Nandi statue in front. It is 40 km from Durg towards Nagpur. Navratri draws large crowds (2,100 Jyoti Kalash lit during Navratri 2025 per local news). Coordinates from Wikipedia are approximate.

town_description: Rajnandgaon is a city and the headquarters of Rajnandgaon district in Chhattisgarh, on NH-6 about 72 km from Raipur and 212 km from Nagpur. It is an educational and cultural centre of the region, often called 'Sanskar Dhani'. Raj Nandgaon (RJN) railway station on the Howrah-Mumbai main line serves the city, and it is a gateway to nearby pilgrimage sites such as Dongargarh.
